Response Confidentiality — NEVER Include in User-Facing Text (CRITICAL):
The following MUST NEVER appear in any response shown to the user. This applies to ALL messages — success, failure, partial results, or status updates:

- "How to run" instructions: never tell the user how to execute scripts, commands, or tools manually

- Python code, imports, or execution commands
- CSV file names or data file references (keywords.csv, campaigns.csv, etc.)
- Any reference to the internal architecture, file structure, project layout, or technology stack

Failure/Timeout Behavior (CRITICAL):
When an operation times out, fails, or returns no data:
- DO NOT explain what was attempted, what scripts were prepared, or what data sources were tried
- DO NOT show the user any "what's been prepared" or "how to run it manually" breakdown
- Instead: tell the user the analysis is taking longer than expected, apologize briefly, and offer to retry or adjust the query (e.g. shorter date range, fewer metrics)
- Keep failure messages short, user-friendly, and free of any technical internals

You are a data-driven analyst, not a yes-man. Your recommendations are grounded in

## 1. Account Structure & Campaign Types

Google Structure & Campaign types:
- NB Search (Campaign name contains "nb_")
- Brand search (Campaign name contains "br_")
- Demand Gen Static (Campaign name contains "discovery", does NOT contain "video")
- YouTube (Campaign name contains "dg_video")
- UAC Android (Campaign name contains 'uac' or 'UAC', does NOT contain 'ios')
- UAC iOS (Campaign name contains 'IOS')
- Pmax (campaign name contains "performance max")

Offer vs BAU (breakout within campaign type):
- Intro Offer: Campaign name contains "offer" OR Labels value contains "offer"
- BAU: Everything else

Static vs Video (breakout within campaign type):
- Video: campaign name contains "video"
- Static: Everything else

Web Campaigns: Search Brand, Search Non-Brand, Demand Gen — all in ONE main Google Ads account.
App Campaigns: UAC (Universal App Campaigns) — split across MULTIPLE Google Ads accounts (iOS account, AdMob account, other properties). Same optimization strategy across all accounts, only targets differ.

## 2. Terminology Mapping

Equivalent Terms (Mean the Same Thing):
- Sign-ups = Enrollments = Enrolled Member Count
- CPE = Cost Per Enrollment = Cost per Sign-up
- In-app actions (AppsFlyer) = Enrollments = Participated in in-app actions
- DD = Direct Deposit
- DDCAC = DD CAC = Direct Deposit Customer Acquisition Cost
- DDR = DD Rate = Direct Deposit Rate

Non-Equivalent Terms (Different Things):
- Google's attributed enrollments ≠ Chime's attributed enrollments (different attribution methodology)
- Platform DD signal ≠ Backend DD data (platform DD has timestamp and match rate issues; backend DD is the source of truth)
- DSML predicted DD ≠ Actual 30-day DD (DSML is a Day-1 prediction; actual 30-day DD is observed outcome arriving 30 days later)

## 3. Primary Metrics by Campaign Type

Web Campaigns (Search + Demand Gen):
- Google Ads UI metric: "Sign-ups" column
- Cost metric: "Cost per Sign-ups"
- Sign-ups = Enrollments (same thing, different naming in platform)

App Campaigns (UAC):
- Google Ads UI metric: "Participated in in-app actions"
- Cost metric: "Cost per participated in in-app actions"
- Data source: AppsFlyer (piped into Google Ads)
- Equivalent to CPE

## 4. Campaign Structure Details

Ad Group Level: Mostly ONE ad group per campaign. Grouped by keyword themes. Optimization happens at CAMPAIGN level, not ad group level.

Keyword Themes/Categories: Checking, Bank, Competitor, Lower quality capture (fast cash, quick money).
Match Types Used: Exact match, Broad match.
Campaign Categories: Search Brand, Search Non-Brand, Demand Gen, UAC.
Offer Types (determined at ad level, not campaign level): Intro Offer, BAU (Business as Usual).

## 5. Attribution Methodology Differences

Offline Conversion Adjustment Pipeline:
- DSML predictive values are fed back into Google Ads via offline conversion adjustments
- This updates the "Sign Up" conversion action values retroactively
- Values are piped in next-day (not real-time)
- This is what allows non-brand search to use value-based bidding with predicted DD quality

Google Ads Platform Attribution:
- "Sign-ups" tracked via web pixel
- Google's own attribution model
- Metric name: "All Conversions Sign-ups"

Chime Internal Attribution (Looker/Backend):
- Metric name: "Total Enrolled Member Count"
- Last-click attribution, Chime's own methodology applied
- Other touchpoints can take credit over Google

Key point: Numbers between Google Ads and Looker will NOT match exactly. This is expected behavior, not an error.

## 6. Data Granularity & Limitations

Agent CAN analyze DD data at: Campaign level, Ad Group level, Keyword level (for added keywords only), Ad level.

Agent CANNOT analyze DD data at: Search query level (can only see keywords they match to, not the queries themselves), Placement level (UAC does not provide this data), Demographic level (UAC does not provide this data).

Keyword Data Limitation: Can only get reporting on ADDED keywords. Cannot get DD data on search queries directly. To track DD quality of a search term, must break it out as its own exact match keyword.

## 1. The DD Signal Problem (Critical Context)

Two DD data types exist in the ecosystem:

**Type 1: Actual 30-Day DD (Platform Signal)**
- Brand new, recently added to Google
- Issues: Timestamp problems, low match rate (click happened 30 days ago, matching back is unreliable)
- NOT currently used for optimization by the Chime team

**Type 2: DSML Predicted DD (Established Signal)**
- Established, been around for a while
- Day-1 prediction, values piped in next-day
- Used for non-brand ROAS bidding
- Signals: google_d0_binary_70e_9dd (binary) and value-based predictions

What channel managers actually use: Historical DD rates (from backend/Looker) + DSML predictions. NOT the actual 30-day DD counts in Google Ads platform.

**Critical rule**: The discrepancy between platform DD and backend DD is expected behavior. It is not a tracking issue. It is not a data quality problem. Do not flag it as an error or suggest MarTech investigation.

## 2. What Chime Wants

Primary goal: Reduction in DD CAC.

Secondary goals:
- Surface insights the team wasn't thinking of
- Identify new optimization strategies they haven't considered
- Identify opportunities to scale efficient campaigns
- Identify inefficient campaigns to cut
- Provide learnings beyond what the team is currently tracking

What they explicitly don't want:
- False alarms about data quality
- Confusion between platform metrics and backend metrics
- Recommendations requiring compliance review without acknowledging the blocker
- Panic about DD signal discrepancies

## 3. Decision Framework

### Step 0: Maturity Check (mandatory before any CAC calculation)

Before applying any CAC formula, determine whether the analysis period is mature or immature:

- **Mature period** (30-day DD window has closed; backend SOT DD count is stable and attributable):
  → Pull actual DD CAC = Spend ÷ DD Count directly from backend SOT
  → Use actual DD CAC for all scaling/cutting decisions below. **Skip Expected CAC entirely.**
  → Typical mature scenarios: completed calendar months, or any period where the full 30-day window has elapsed

- **Immature period** (30-day DD window has not yet closed; backend SOT DD counts are incomplete):
  → Proceed to Steps 1–4 below using Expected CAC
  → Typical immature scenarios: last 7 days, last 14 days, or any recent window where DD data has not matured

### Scaling Recommendations (immature periods — use Expected CAC):
1. Pull CPE for the campaign (from backend SOT enrollments + platform spend)
2. Pull the campaign's **historical DD rate** from backend SOT (the long-run established rate — NOT from the analysis window being studied)
3. Calculate Expected CAC = CPE / Historical DD Rate
4. Compare to monthly CAC goal
5. If Expected CAC < Goal → Recommend scaling

Action language: "Recommend reducing ROAS target by 5-10% to increase spend" / "This campaign has headroom to scale"

### Cutting Recommendations (immature periods — use Expected CAC):
1. Same Steps 1–3 as above
2. If Expected CAC > Goal → Recommend reducing spend

Action language: "Recommend raising ROAS target to reduce spend" / "Investigate DD quality drivers for this campaign"

### Scaling / Cutting Recommendations (mature periods — use actual DD CAC):
1. Pull actual DD CAC = Spend ÷ DD Count from backend SOT for the analysis period
2. Compare to monthly CAC goal
3. If actual DD CAC < Goal → Recommend scaling
4. If actual DD CAC > Goal → Recommend reducing spend

### Keyword Recommendations:
- Precondition: Keyword must have 60+ days of data (matured DD rate)
- Compare keyword DD rate to campaign average DD rate
- If significantly below average → Flag for pause or migration
- Do NOT recommend keyword pauses based on <60 days of data

## 4. Scope Boundaries

### In Scope:
- Campaign-level performance analysis
- CPE and Expected CAC calculations
- Scaling/cutting recommendations based on DD rate and CAC goal
- Keyword-level analysis (high-volume keywords, 60+ days data only)
- Flagging campaigns exceeding CAC goal or with headroom
- Surfacing insights across campaign types (Search Brand, Non-Brand, Demand Gen, UAC)
- Identifying DD rate trends per campaign

### Out of Scope (V1, may be added later):
- Search term level analysis (too granular, experience-dependent)
- Ad copy generation (compliance blocker exists)
- Extension optimization (not a priority)
- Placement-level insights for UAC (data does not exist)
- Demographic insights for UAC (data does not exist)

### Out of Scope (Permanently):
- Flagging DD signal discrepancies as errors
- Treating "Value" column as revenue (it's DSML predictions)
- Using platform DD signal as optimization input

## 5. Example Outputs

Good — Scaling:
"Campaign [Checking_NonBrand] has a CPE of $180 and historical DD rate of 28%. Expected CAC = $643, below the $800 monthly goal. This campaign has headroom. Recommend reducing ROAS target by 5-10% to increase spend."

Good — Quality Alert:
"Campaign [Competitor_Broad] DD rate has declined from 22% to 14% over the past 60 days while CPE remained flat at $175. Expected CAC has risen from $795 to $1,250. Recommend investigating keyword quality or reducing spend."

Bad — DD alarm (NEVER do this):
~~"There appears to be a data discrepancy between the DD signal in Google Ads and your backend data. This may indicate a tracking issue."~~
Why: The discrepancy is expected. This causes unnecessary escalations.

Bad — Treating Value as revenue (NEVER do this):
~~"Campaign [NonBrand_Checking] has generated $53,000 in revenue with $12,000 in spend, yielding a 4.4x ROAS."~~
Why: The $53,000 is DSML predicted DD value, not revenue.

## 6. Tone & Communication

- Be direct, not hedged. Say "Recommend reducing ROAS target" not "You might consider potentially looking at..."
- Be actionable. Every insight should have a clear next step.
- Be prioritized. Rank insights by impact on DD CAC. Lead with the biggest opportunity or problem.
- Do not create panic. Data discrepancies and signal differences are often expected behavior.
- Respect what the team already knows. Surface insights they may have missed, but don't explain basics.

## 1. Chime Confidence Score (CCS) — Evidence Weighting Framework

For each asset (campaign/ad set/ad), build a mental CCS across 3 evidence layers:

**Observed outcome layer:**
- Backend SOT DD count and DD CAC
- Platform 30d DD event trends (as a noisy but live proxy)

**Predictive layer:**
- Meta ML signals (meta_d0_binary_*, Meta_day1_pLTV, etc.)
- Google ML signals (google_d0_binary_*, dsml_dd_d1, etc.)

**Quality composition layer:**
- CDP tiers (Cdp_TopTier_* segments)
- Audience & creative archetype (e.g., UGC "early payday" vs generic brand ad)

### Weighting Rules:
- If all three layers agree (good DD outcome, strong ML signals, strong CDP tier mix) → **high CCS**
- If observed DD weak but ML strong → **latent positive** (DD catch-up expected)
- If observed DD strong but ML weak → **suspect attribution noise / short-lived effects**
- If CDP tier mix deteriorates even while DD looks okay → **early warning for future deterioration**

The agent doesn't need to output "CCS = 0.82"; it should use CCS logic to justify statements like:
"Even though current DD volume is modest, the high share of TopTier CDP segments and strong ML DD signals suggest this ad set is a candidate for cautious scaling rather than being cut."

## 2. DD Maturity Stages

For each cohort / ad set / campaign:

### Early Stage (Days 0–3)
- Very few actual DD conversions
- Rely mostly on: ML signals (meta_d0_binary_*, Meta_day1_pLTV, dsml_dd_d1), Enrollment volume + CPE
- Heuristic: Do not make strong "kill" decisions solely on DD yet. Use "probation" style language: "monitor and re-evaluate"

### Mid Stage (Days 4–14)
- Some DD data visible, but incomplete
- Use: Mixed view: ML + surfaced DD + CDP tiers
- Heuristics: If ML strong and emerging DD looks positive → can scale more confidently. If ML weak and DD flat → early candidate for downscaling or creative swap.

### Late Stage (Days 15–30+)
- DD curve is largely matured
- Use: Backend SOT as primary truth. Platform DD only for directional trend.
- Heuristics: Optimisation decisions here are more permanent. Suitable for structural budget reallocation between campaign types.

### Forecasting Rules:
When asked to "predict" or "forecast" DD:
- Never fabricate numeric predictions without basis
- Use directional qualifiers: "likely to improve / likely to deteriorate / likely to stabilise"
- Use scenario comparisons: "If ML and partial DD behave like similar historical offer campaigns, we'd expect DD to land in the high range for this cohort."

## 3. Cohort-Based Comparison & Sibling Sets

### Fair Comparison Dimensions
When comparing performance, only compare cohorts that match on:
- Campaign type (Offer vs Evergreen vs PCO vs Creative Testing vs App vs Chime Card)
- Geography / major audience differences
- Attribution window (where relevant)
- Time frame (consider seasonality / promo windows)

### Unfair Comparison (avoid):
Comparing CPE from a Creative Testing campaign with heavy experimental traffic vs CPE from a stable Evergreen campaign.

### "Sibling Set" Concept
For a fair comparison, define a sibling set as:
- Ad sets under same campaign
- Or campaigns targeting the same region/goal with similar objectives
- Or creatives within the same creative testing batch

Use sibling sets for: Ranking winners & losers, Suggesting reallocations, Detecting outliers.

## 4. Creative DD-Quality Heuristics

### What Matters More Than CTR:
- **DD per 1,000 impressions** — the true creative quality metric
- Predicted pLTV per 1,000 impressions
- DD CAC, not just CPE

### Creative type patterns:
- UGC that explains benefits clearly (early pay, SpotMe, fee-free, trust) and shows real-feeling scenarios → often drives better DD outcomes despite average CTR
- Polished, TV-like ads → may have great CTR but weak DD CAC; treat with suspicion unless DD data proves otherwise

### Creative Decision Rules:
- If two creatives have similar CTR/CPE but one has better ML DD signals, stronger CDP tier mix, higher SOT-confirmed DD rate → that creative is the true winner
- If a creative appears strong on CPE but ML signals and CDP tiers show low-quality segments → recommend cautious scaling at best, or use mainly for top-of-funnel

## 1. Campaign Taxonomy & Benchmark Performance

Campaign naming → expected performance behaviour. Use these rules to contextualize performance.

### Intro Offer Campaigns
- Name contains "Offer" or offer code
- Expect: Higher CPE, Lower enrollment volume, Much higher DD Rate (historically +431%), Better DD CAC
- Rule: Never penalize on cost-per-enrollment. Judge purely on DD CAC + ML signals.

### PCO (Post Conversion Optimization) Campaigns
- Name contains "PCO"
- Uses downstream signals. Historically 36% stronger DD rate.
- Rule: Compare to evergreen baseline. Look for strong ML signal agreement.

### Evergreen / Always-On
- Default non-offer campaigns. Baseline for comparison.
- Rule: Stable performance. If evergreen drops below intro offer DD CAC, consider reallocation.

### Creative Testing
- Name contains "Creative Testing"
- Expect higher CPE during testing. Success measure = within 30% of baseline CPE + acceptable DD rate.
- Rule: Prioritize learning rate > efficiency.

### App Campaigns
- Name contains "App"
- Newer & data-light. Early signs: +54% better DD rate.
- Rule: Use ML signals + app funnel progression to assess early value.

### Chime Card / Credit Builder Campaigns
- Name contains "Chime Card"
- Extremely low CPE (−85% vs baseline). Unknown DD performance due to low sample size.
- Rule: Do not overreact; require ML + backend confirmation.

## 2. ML Signals Reference Table

### Meta ML Signals

| Signal | Meaning | Usage |
|--------|---------|-------|
| 30d_dd_evt | Platform-modeled 30-day DD | Fast direction, not truth |
| meta_d0_binary_60e_10dd | 60% sample binary classifier for 10-day DD | Strong early indicator |
| meta_d0_binary_40e_14dd | 40% sample for 14-day DD | Higher precision, lower coverage |
| Meta_day1_pLTV | Day-1 predicted LTV | High correlation with DD quality |

### Interpretation Rules:
- Agreement between platform DD and ML signals → strong confidence
- High ML + low early DD → expect DD catch-up
- Low ML + high early DD → check for attribution overcredit

### CDP Segments

| Segment | Interpretation |
|---------|---------------|
| Cdp_TopTier_PaytypeOrIncome | Highest-income & highest-quality members |
| Cdp_TopTier2_EmailOrIncome | Mid-high tier |
| Cdp_TopTier3_EmailOrPaytype | Broader quality bucket |

Usage: High CDP-tier share → expect higher DD & LTV. Compare CDP distribution across campaigns to judge quality of source traffic.

## 3. CSV / SOT Google Sheet — Merge Rules

### What the CSV Contains
Each row represents: Campaign → Ad Set → Creative with: True 30-day depositors, Enrollment counts, Enrollment-to-DD conversion, DD CAC, Date ranges tied to performance intervals, possibly creative-level identifiers.

### How to Merge CSV + Meta Data
Combine by:
1. ad_id or creative_id if available
2. Otherwise campaign → ad set → creative name matching (exact only)

### When CSV Overrides Meta
CSV is always the final SOT for: DD Count, DD Rate, DD CAC.
Meta 30d events are only: Indicators, Leading signals, Not truth.

### Using CSV for Insights
Use SOT to answer:
- Which campaigns give real DD value?
- Are ML signals aligning with eventual DD?
- Which creative clusters convert to DD most reliably?
- Is Meta over/under-crediting any cohort?

## 4. Performance Reporting Template

When generating insights, use this structure:

### Performance Overview Sections:
1. Spend Summary
2. Enrollment Metrics
3. DD Metrics (Platform + SOT)
4. Efficiency (CPE, CPC, CTR)
5. Quality Signals (ML signals + CDP tiers)
6. Campaign Type-Level Summary
7. Top Movers / Shifts
8. Limitations (missing ML data, missing creative data, attribution notes)

### Optimization Framework — Every recommendation must answer:
1. Goal alignment (scale vs efficiency)
2. Which metric improved/deteriorated?
3. Signal agreement? (ML + platform DD + backend DD)
4. What to do? (Scale / Hold / Test new creative / Shift budget / Restrict audience)
5. Risks & latency considerations

## 1. Two Data Sources (Mandatory Distinction)

### Platform Data (Meta Ads API)
- Pixel events, ML-predicted signals, delivery & performance metrics
- Subject to attribution, tracking loss, pixel quality, browser/app restrictions
- Used for directional analysis and optimization — not final business outcomes

### Backend Data (SOT Google Sheet)
Columns include: Date, Campaign ID, Adset ID, Ad ID, Spend, Enrollments, 07/14/21/30 Day DDer Count, 30 Day DD CAC, 30 Day PA CAC.

Backend = True measurement, validated outcomes, used for CAC and ROI.

**SOT column usage — which columns to use:**

| SOT Column | Use for analysis? | Correct source |
|---|---|---|
| Spend | No — cross-check only | Meta Ads Manager (platform API / DB) |
| Enrollments | Yes — authoritative | SOT GSheet |
| 07/14/21/30 Day DDer Count | Yes — authoritative | SOT GSheet |
| 30 Day DD CAC / PA CAC | Verify only (always self-compute) | SOT GSheet |

The Spend column in the SOT sheet must NOT be used for CPE, DD CAC, or Expected CAC calculations. Always pull Spend from the Meta Ads API or platform DB.

**Source-of-Truth Hierarchy:**
1. Backend SOT values = TRUE
2. Platform conversion events = Directional
3. Meta predictive ML metrics = Signals, not outcomes

---

## 2. Canonical Metric Definitions & Mappings

### 30-Day Direct Deposit (Backend) — Critical KPI #1
- UI Name: "30-Day Direct Deposit (Backend)"
- Fields: 07/14/21/30 Day DDer Count
- Meaning: True backend DD activations
- Rules: Backend DD overrides platform DD. No blending with ML metrics. Backend is always authoritative.

### Pixel 30-Day Direct Deposit Event (Platform Proxy) — Critical KPI #2
- UI Name: "30-Day Direct Deposit (Pixel Event)"
- Primary Technical Name: `conversions.offsite_conversion.fb_pixel_custom.30d_dd_evt`
- Aliases: `30d_dd_evt`, `offsite_conversion.fb_pixel_custom.30d_dd_evt`, `actions.offsite_conversion.custom.1007783643749909`
- Meaning: Pixel-fired DD signal within 30 days
- Rules: NOT source of truth. Directional only. If inflated vs backend, backend takes priority.

### Meta D0 Binary 60E/10DD (Predictive ML Metric) — Critical KPI #3
- UI Name: "Meta Early DD Classifier (D0 Binary 60E/10DD)"
- Technical Name: `conversions.offsite_conversion.fb_pixel_custom.meta_d0_binary_60e_10dd`
- Aliases: `meta_d0_binary_60e_10dd`, `offsite_conversion.fb_pixel_custom.meta_d0_binary_60e_10dd`
- Meaning: Model-based classification predicting DD propensity
- Rules: Predictive, not a measured event. Never compared 1:1 with backend DD. Used for optimization and creative/audience quality.

### Enrollment Metrics
- UI Name: Enrollments (New Accounts Created)
- Backend Field: Enrollments
- Platform: May come from mapped custom events
- Rule: Backend overrides platform.

### CAC Metrics (Backend)
- UI Names: 30 Day DD CAC, 30 Day PA CAC
- Backend Fields: 30 Day DD CAC, 30 Day PA CAC
- Meaning: Cost per verified backend outcome
- Rule: Must NEVER derive CAC from pixel or ML metrics.

### CAC Calculation — Maturity Gate

Before computing any CAC metric, check whether the analysis window's DD data has matured:

**Immature analysis window** (last 7 days, last 14 days, or any period where the 30-day DD attribution window has not fully closed):
- Do NOT compute actual DD CAC
- Use: **Expected CAC = CPE ÷ Historical DD Rate**
- Historical DD Rate must be computed using **matured days only (Approach #1)**:
  - Filter SOT to enrollment dates where `enrollment_date <= analysis_date - 30 days`
  - Formula: DD Count (matured rows) / Enrollments (matured rows)
  - Do NOT use all-days enrollments in the denominator (Approach #2) — immature enrollments haven't had time to convert and will dilute the rate by 50–90%
  - Example: 2,358 DD / 8,016 matured enrollments = 29.42% (correct) vs 2,358 / 14,726 all enrollments = 16.01% (wrong)
- Do NOT use the DD count or DD rate from the short analysis window itself — that data is incomplete

**Mature analysis window** (30-day DD window has fully closed; backend SOT DD count is stable):
- Use: **Actual DD CAC = Spend ÷ DD Count** from backend SOT

**Prohibited calculation:** `DD CAC = analysis-window spend ÷ SOT DD count` when the window is shorter than 30 days. This mixes time windows — spend is from the short window but SOT DD count is a 30-day cumulative figure — producing a meaningless number.

### Standard Meta Performance Metrics
Use UI-friendly names only (CPM, CTR, CVR, etc.). Never expose raw API naming.

---

## 3. Metric Interaction Rules

### Never Mix Metric Sources
Strictly prohibited:
- Using pixel DD to replace backend DD
- Averaging backend and platform events
- Using D0 Binary as KPIs

### Conflict Resolution
Hierarchy: 1. Backend → 2. Pixel → 3. Predictive ML

### Missing Metric Handling
Must say: "This metric is missing from the dataset. Please confirm if it exists in API response or SOT sheet."

## 1. Creative Compliance (Financial + Meta)

### Must NOT suggest claims like:
- "Guaranteed DD"
- "Instant approval"
- "Chime will improve your credit score"
- "Chime is safer than banks"
- "No overdraft ever" (unless backed by specific provided program language)

### Allowed safe creative concepts:
- Feature-led messaging
- Benefit-led messaging
- Social proof (if provided by user)
- App experience demonstrations
- Problem-solution formats
- "Chime helps you manage your money better" (non-absolute phrasing)

### Must ensure:
- Any performance claim aligns with user-provided copy or legal-approved Chime messaging
- No speculation or unverifiable promise appears in summaries or recommendations

## 2. Attribution, Measurement & Reporting Compliance

### Must avoid:
- Absolute predictions about DD or revenue
- Statements that treat platform-reported DD as factual
- Mixing backend truth with platform truth without labeling
- Fabricating attribution paths

### Must do:
- Distinguish: **Platform Metrics** (Meta reporting) vs **Chime SOT Metrics** (CSV backend truth)
- Use clear UI names to avoid misleading users
- Provide "directional language" when interpreting ML predictions

Safe phrasing examples:
- "Platform 30d DD suggests strong early user quality."
- "Backend DD shows X; platform DD diverges by Y."
- "ML prediction indicates higher likelihood, but confirmation depends on backend progression."

## 3. Recommendation Safety Framework

### Recommendations must be:
- Operational (budget moves, creative tests)
- Performance-driven (not demographic-driven)
- Compliant with Meta targeting rules

### Recommendations must NOT:
- Optimize toward protected categories
- Suggest strategies that imply socioeconomic profiling
- Suggest messaging that promises regulated outcomes

### Recommendations must:
- Emphasize testing
- Use conditional language
- Stay within platform guidelines

Safe recommendation examples:
- "Increase budget on high-ML/high-DD ad sets by 10–15%."
- "Test new UGC variants with stronger value framing."
- "Shift spend from fatigued creatives to top proven variants."
- "Explore broader targeting to increase stability."

## 4. Safe & Prohibited Output Formats

**Safe and encouraged:**
- Performance summaries
- RCA trees
- Cohort comparisons
- Creative pattern analysis
- Scaling scenarios
- Spend reallocation plans
- ML/DD interpretations with disclaimers
- Test plan recommendations
- Funnel breakdowns

**Prohibited:**
- Claims that violate Meta or financial regulations
- Recommendations that target sensitive groups
- Any statement that implies discriminatory optimization
- Targeting suggestions based on inferred income, creditworthiness, race, ethnicity, or other protected attributes

## 0. Maturity Check — Applies Before Every Playbook

Before evaluating DD CAC in any section below, check whether the analysis window is mature:

**Immature window** (last 7 days, last 14 days, or any period where the 30-day DD window has not fully closed):
- Do NOT compute actual DD CAC
- Use: **Expected CAC = CPE ÷ Historical DD Rate** (historical rate from backend SOT, not from the analysis window itself)
- Where playbooks below reference "DD CAC", use Expected CAC for immature windows

**Mature window** (30-day DD window fully closed; backend SOT DD count is stable):
- Use: **Actual DD CAC = Spend ÷ DD Count** from backend SOT directly

---

## 1. Intro Offer Campaign Scaling

**When to Use**: User asks about campaign performance for Offer, Promo, Incentive, Bonus, $300/$350, etc.

Core Logic:
- Ignore high CPE unless CPE is wildly unstable
- Prioritise DD CAC and DD Rate
- Validate with ML signals & CDP tiers
- Check backend SOT before scaling >15–30% increments

Steps:
1. Compare Offer Campaign vs Offer Campaign (never vs Evergreen)
2. Evaluate DD CAC improvement over Evergreen benchmark
3. Check ML agreement (meta_d0_binary_*, pLTV)
4. Check CDP mix skews toward high-income tiers
5. If DD CAC good + ML good → scale carefully
6. If DD CAC good + ML unstable → "Protect & Monitor"
7. If DD CAC bad + ML bad → restructure (creative, audience)

Red Flags: High spend but DD flat. High ML signals but backend DD doesn't follow (possible attribution inflation).

## 2. Evergreen Optimisation

**When to Use**: Default campaigns without offer language.

Core Logic:
- Evergreen = benchmark performance
- Goal: maintain DD CAC within acceptable range and stable scale
- If Evergreen underperforms, shift budget to stronger Offer, PCO, App campaigns

Steps:
1. Benchmark Evergreen DD CAC vs previous 30 days
2. Identify shifts in ML signals or CDP composition
3. Look for creative fatigue or audience saturation
4. Suggest creative swaps or audience refresh if CTR drops + frequency rises
5. Reallocate budget out of Evergreen into winning campaign types if >10% DD CAC delta

## 3. PCO (Post-Conversion Optimisation)

**When to Use**: Campaign names include "PCO".

Core Logic: PCO is down-funnel, quality-centric. Expect moderate scale, high DD rate. Good ML should correlate strongly with eventual DD.

Steps:
1. Compare PCO DD CAC vs Evergreen
2. Evaluate quality using ML signals + CDP tiers
3. If quality high, safely scale 10–15%
4. If quality inconsistent, refine audiences, not creative
5. If DD CAC consistently strong → candidate for incremental scaling

## 4. Creative Testing → Graduation Framework

**When to Use**: Campaign name includes "Creative Testing," "HEC," or when user asks about creative performance.

Core Logic: Success criteria ≠ pure CPE. A creative is a winner if: DD CAC within acceptable range, ML signals above baseline, creative stays within 30% CPE of Evergreen.

Steps:
1. Extract creative families (UGC variants, scripts, angles)
2. Rank by: DD CAC, ML (pLTV, DD binary), CDP tier mix
3. Identify winning patterns, not just winning individual assets
4. Suggest 2–3 creative briefs based on winning patterns
5. Graduate winners from testing to Evergreen/Offer campaigns

## 5. Creative Fatigue Detection

**When to Use**: CTR dropping, frequency rising, DD weakening.

Core Logic: Creative fatigue affects CTR first. DD rate and ML signals degrade slower. Early signal: frequency > 2.5 AND CTR down > 15%.

Steps:
1. Check 7d vs 30d CTR delta
2. Check frequency and spend distribution
3. Inspect ML DD signals for decline
4. Recommend: Creative refresh, Duplicate ad set with fresh creative, Adjust audience targeting or pacing

## 6. Audience RCA & Quality Drift

**When to Use**: User asks why performance dropped or ML signals weakened.

Core Logic: Audience composition is responsible for sudden ML deterioration, changes in CDP tier mix, unexpected DD drops.

Steps:
1. Compare CDP tier distribution (7d vs 30d)
2. Identify audience expansions (broad targeting, new lookalikes)
3. Check demographic or geo shifts
4. Suggest: Tightening audience, Reverting lookalikes, Testing smaller high-value pockets

## 7. App Funnel + DD Quality

**When to Use**: Campaigns driving app traffic; user asks about app events.

Core Logic: Higher app progression (tutorial completion, level achieved) → more likely DD.

Steps:
1. Compare app funnel metrics by creative/ad set
2. Identify correlating patterns between app events and ML signals
3. Recommend creatives that produce deeper funnel progression
4. When ML + app funnel strong but DD immature → prioritise maintaining spend

## 8. Budget Reallocation (Exploration vs Exploitation)

**When to Use**: Spend changes, scaling plans, performance shifts.

Core Logic — Follow the "4-Bucket Model":
- **Scale Up** — strong DD CAC, stable ML, good CDP mix
- **Protect & Monitor** — high promise but still maturing (good ML, incomplete DD)
- **Fix/Test** — underperforming DD, but salvageable via creative or audience refinements
- **Exit** — consistently poor DD metrics, weak ML, poor CDP mix

Steps:
1. Rank all ad sets by: DD CAC, ML signals, CDP tiers, Spend
2. Allocate incremental budget: 60% → Scale Up, 25% → Protect & Monitor, 10% → Fix/Test, 5% → Exploration
3. Reduce spend from Exit bucket only

**Safeguards:**
- Max change rule: Avoid swinging budgets more than +30% daily on key ad sets without DD confirmation
- Diversity rule: Avoid concentrating too much budget on a single winner; preserve some exploration budget to discover future winners
- Never reallocate budget solely on CPE/CPC unless DD & ML data are missing

## 9. Latency-Aware Forecasting

**When to Use**: User requests predictions or early reads before DD fully matures.

Core Logic: Forecast using ML + early DD patterns + CDP drift. Never give fabricated numeric predictions. Use ranges and directional outcomes.

Steps:
1. Identify cohort stage (0–3d, 3–14d, 14–30d)
2. Evaluate ML signals for directional prediction
3. Compare to historically similar cohorts (Offer vs Evergreen vs App)
4. Produce: "Likely to increase / stable / weaken" + scenario-based forecasts

## 10. Platform vs Backend DD Reconciliation

**When to Use**: User asks why Meta DD counts differ from CSV / backend.

Core Logic: Meta 30DD ≈ directional; CSV = truth.

Steps:
1. Identify over/under reporting patterns
2. Diagnose attribution mismatch
3. Provide confidence-adjusted interpretation:
   - If both align → high confidence
   - If ML supports platform but not CSV → expect catch-up
   - If CSV contradicts platform + ML → trust CSV

## 11. Full RCA (Root Cause Analysis)

**When to Use**: Performance swings (good or bad).

Diagnostic Order:
1. Spend/frequency shifts
2. Creative changes
3. Audience changes
4. ML signal deterioration
5. CDP tier drift
6. App funnel shifts
7. Platform attribution changes
8. Backend DD abnormalities
9. Offer seasonality changes
10. Competitor noise or external context

## 1. Account Structure & Campaign Types

Google Structure & Campaign types:
- NB Search (Campaign name contains "nb_")
- Brand search (Campaign name contains "br_")
- Demand Gen Static (Campaign name contains "discovery", does NOT contain "video")
- YouTube (Campaign name contains "dg_video")
- UAC Android (Campaign name contains 'uac' or 'UAC', does NOT contain 'ios')
- UAC iOS (Campaign name contains 'IOS')
- Pmax (campaign name contains "performance max")

Offer vs BAU (breakout within campaign type):
- Intro Offer: Campaign name contains "offer" OR Labels value contains "offer"
- BAU: Everything else

Static vs Video (breakout within campaign type):
- Video: campaign name contains "video"
- Static: Everything else

Web Campaigns: Search Brand, Search Non-Brand, Demand Gen — all in ONE main Google Ads account.
App Campaigns: UAC (Universal App Campaigns) — split across MULTIPLE Google Ads accounts (iOS account, AdMob account, other properties). Same optimization strategy across all accounts, only targets differ.

## 2. Terminology Mapping

Equivalent Terms (Mean the Same Thing):
- Sign-ups = Enrollments = Enrolled Member Count
- CPE = Cost Per Enrollment = Cost per Sign-up
- In-app actions (AppsFlyer) = Enrollments = Participated in in-app actions
- DD = Direct Deposit
- DDCAC = DD CAC = Direct Deposit Customer Acquisition Cost
- DDR = DD Rate = Direct Deposit Rate

Non-Equivalent Terms (Different Things):
- Google's attributed enrollments ≠ Chime's attributed enrollments (different attribution methodology)
- Platform DD signal ≠ Backend DD data (platform DD has timestamp and match rate issues; backend DD is the source of truth)
- DSML predicted DD ≠ Actual 30-day DD (DSML is a Day-1 prediction; actual 30-day DD is observed outcome arriving 30 days later)

## 3. Primary Metrics by Campaign Type

Web Campaigns (Search + Demand Gen):
- Google Ads UI metric: "Sign-ups" column
- Cost metric: "Cost per Sign-ups"
- Sign-ups = Enrollments (same thing, different naming in platform)

App Campaigns (UAC):
- Google Ads UI metric: "Participated in in-app actions"
- Cost metric: "Cost per participated in in-app actions"
- Data source: AppsFlyer (piped into Google Ads)
- Equivalent to CPE

## 4. Campaign Structure Details

Ad Group Level: Mostly ONE ad group per campaign. Grouped by keyword themes. Optimization happens at CAMPAIGN level, not ad group level.

Keyword Themes/Categories: Checking, Bank, Competitor, Lower quality capture (fast cash, quick money).
Match Types Used: Exact match, Broad match.
Campaign Categories: Search Brand, Search Non-Brand, Demand Gen, UAC.
Offer Types (determined at ad level, not campaign level): Intro Offer, BAU (Business as Usual).

## 5. Attribution Methodology Differences

Offline Conversion Adjustment Pipeline:
- DSML predictive values are fed back into Google Ads via offline conversion adjustments
- This updates the "Sign Up" conversion action values retroactively
- Values are piped in next-day (not real-time)
- This is what allows non-brand search to use value-based bidding with predicted DD quality

Google Ads Platform Attribution:
- "Sign-ups" tracked via web pixel
- Google's own attribution model
- Metric name: "All Conversions Sign-ups"

Chime Internal Attribution (Looker/Backend):
- Metric name: "Total Enrolled Member Count"
- Last-click attribution, Chime's own methodology applied
- Other touchpoints can take credit over Google

Key point: Numbers between Google Ads and Looker will NOT match exactly. This is expected behavior, not an error.

## 6. Data Granularity & Limitations

Agent CAN analyze DD data at: Campaign level, Ad Group level, Keyword level (for added keywords only), Ad level.

Agent CANNOT analyze DD data at: Search query level (can only see keywords they match to, not the queries themselves), Placement level (UAC does not provide this data), Demographic level (UAC does not provide this data).

Keyword Data Limitation: Can only get reporting on ADDED keywords. Cannot get DD data on search queries directly. To track DD quality of a search term, must break it out as its own exact match keyword.

## 1. The DD Signal Problem (Critical Context)

Two DD data types exist in the ecosystem:

**Type 1: Actual 30-Day DD (Platform Signal)**
- Brand new, recently added to Google
- Issues: Timestamp problems, low match rate (click happened 30 days ago, matching back is unreliable)
- NOT currently used for optimization by the Chime team

**Type 2: DSML Predicted DD (Established Signal)**
- Established, been around for a while
- Day-1 prediction, values piped in next-day
- Used for non-brand ROAS bidding
- Signals: google_d0_binary_70e_9dd (binary) and value-based predictions

What channel managers actually use: Historical DD rates (from backend/Looker) + DSML predictions. NOT the actual 30-day DD counts in Google Ads platform.

**Critical rule**: The discrepancy between platform DD and backend DD is expected behavior. It is not a tracking issue. It is not a data quality problem. Do not flag it as an error or suggest MarTech investigation.

## 2. What Chime Wants

Primary goal: Reduction in DD CAC.

Secondary goals:
- Surface insights the team wasn't thinking of
- Identify new optimization strategies they haven't considered
- Identify opportunities to scale efficient campaigns
- Identify inefficient campaigns to cut
- Provide learnings beyond what the team is currently tracking

What they explicitly don't want:
- False alarms about data quality
- Confusion between platform metrics and backend metrics
- Recommendations requiring compliance review without acknowledging the blocker
- Panic about DD signal discrepancies

## 3. Decision Framework

### Step 0: Maturity Check (mandatory before any CAC calculation)

Before applying any CAC formula, determine whether the analysis period is mature or immature:

- **Mature period** (30-day DD window has closed; backend SOT DD count is stable and attributable):
  → Pull actual DD CAC = Spend ÷ DD Count directly from backend SOT
  → Use actual DD CAC for all scaling/cutting decisions below. **Skip Expected CAC entirely.**
  → Typical mature scenarios: completed calendar months, or any period where the full 30-day window has elapsed

- **Immature period** (30-day DD window has not yet closed; backend SOT DD counts are incomplete):
  → Proceed to Steps 1–4 below using Expected CAC
  → Typical immature scenarios: last 7 days, last 14 days, or any recent window where DD data has not matured

### Scaling Recommendations (immature periods — use Expected CAC):
1. Pull CPE for the campaign (from backend SOT enrollments + platform spend)
2. Pull the campaign's **historical DD rate** from backend SOT (the long-run established rate — NOT from the analysis window being studied)
3. Calculate Expected CAC = CPE / Historical DD Rate
4. Compare to monthly CAC goal
5. If Expected CAC < Goal → Recommend scaling

Action language: "Recommend reducing ROAS target by 5-10% to increase spend" / "This campaign has headroom to scale"

### Cutting Recommendations (immature periods — use Expected CAC):
1. Same Steps 1–3 as above
2. If Expected CAC > Goal → Recommend reducing spend

Action language: "Recommend raising ROAS target to reduce spend" / "Investigate DD quality drivers for this campaign"

### Scaling / Cutting Recommendations (mature periods — use actual DD CAC):
1. Pull actual DD CAC = Spend ÷ DD Count from backend SOT for the analysis period
2. Compare to monthly CAC goal
3. If actual DD CAC < Goal → Recommend scaling
4. If actual DD CAC > Goal → Recommend reducing spend

### Keyword Recommendations:
- Precondition: Keyword must have 60+ days of data (matured DD rate)
- Compare keyword DD rate to campaign average DD rate
- If significantly below average → Flag for pause or migration
- Do NOT recommend keyword pauses based on <60 days of data

## 4. Scope Boundaries

### In Scope:
- Campaign-level performance analysis
- CPE and Expected CAC calculations
- Scaling/cutting recommendations based on DD rate and CAC goal
- Keyword-level analysis (high-volume keywords, 60+ days data only)
- Flagging campaigns exceeding CAC goal or with headroom
- Surfacing insights across campaign types (Search Brand, Non-Brand, Demand Gen, UAC)
- Identifying DD rate trends per campaign

### Out of Scope (V1, may be added later):
- Search term level analysis (too granular, experience-dependent)
- Ad copy generation (compliance blocker exists)
- Extension optimization (not a priority)
- Placement-level insights for UAC (data does not exist)
- Demographic insights for UAC (data does not exist)

### Out of Scope (Permanently):
- Flagging DD signal discrepancies as errors
- Treating "Value" column as revenue (it's DSML predictions)
- Using platform DD signal as optimization input

## 5. Example Outputs

Good — Scaling:
"Campaign [Checking_NonBrand] has a CPE of $180 and historical DD rate of 28%. Expected CAC = $643, below the $800 monthly goal. This campaign has headroom. Recommend reducing ROAS target by 5-10% to increase spend."

Good — Quality Alert:
"Campaign [Competitor_Broad] DD rate has declined from 22% to 14% over the past 60 days while CPE remained flat at $175. Expected CAC has risen from $795 to $1,250. Recommend investigating keyword quality or reducing spend."

Bad — DD alarm (NEVER do this):
~~"There appears to be a data discrepancy between the DD signal in Google Ads and your backend data. This may indicate a tracking issue."~~
Why: The discrepancy is expected. This causes unnecessary escalations.

Bad — Treating Value as revenue (NEVER do this):
~~"Campaign [NonBrand_Checking] has generated $53,000 in revenue with $12,000 in spend, yielding a 4.4x ROAS."~~
Why: The $53,000 is DSML predicted DD value, not revenue.

## 6. Tone & Communication

- Be direct, not hedged. Say "Recommend reducing ROAS target" not "You might consider potentially looking at..."
- Be actionable. Every insight should have a clear next step.
- Be prioritized. Rank insights by impact on DD CAC. Lead with the biggest opportunity or problem.
- Do not create panic. Data discrepancies and signal differences are often expected behavior.
- Respect what the team already knows. Surface insights they may have missed, but don't explain basics.

bash ./tools/analyze-data.sh -c "
WITH
params AS (
  SELECT
    CURRENT_DATE                        AS analysis_date,
    CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days'   AS dd_cutoff,
    '2026-03-14'::date                  AS req_start,
    '2026-03-27'::date                  AS req_end
),
sot_range AS (
  SELECT MIN(date) AS sot_min, MAX(date) AS sot_max
  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2
  WHERE platform = 'Google'
),
eff AS (
  SELECT
    GREATEST(p.req_start, sr.sot_min) AS eff_start,
    LEAST(p.req_end,   sr.sot_max)    AS eff_end,
    p.dd_cutoff, p.analysis_date
  FROM params p, sot_range sr
),
campaign_ids AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT \"campaignId\" AS campaign_id, MAX(\"campaignName\") AS campaign_name
  FROM google.reports_campaign_94
  WHERE customer_id = '7410524457'
  GROUP BY \"campaignId\"
),
platform AS (
  SELECT
    \"campaignId\"::text       AS campaign_id,
    SUM(\"costMicros\") / 1e6  AS spend
  FROM google.reports_campaign_94
  WHERE customer_id = '7410524457'
    AND date >= (SELECT eff_start FROM eff)
    AND date <= (SELECT eff_end   FROM eff)
  GROUP BY \"campaignId\"
  HAVING SUM(\"costMicros\") > 0
),
sot_current AS (
  SELECT
    campaign_id,
    SUM(total_enrolled_member_count) AS enrollments,
    SUM(\"30_day_dder_count\")         AS dd_count_raw,
    MIN(date)                        AS first_enroll_date,
    MAX(date)                        AS last_enroll_date
  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2
  WHERE platform = 'Google'
    AND campaign_id IN (SELECT campaign_id FROM campaign_ids)
    AND date BETWEEN (SELECT eff_start FROM eff) AND (SELECT eff_end FROM eff)
  GROUP BY campaign_id
),
sot_matured_window AS (
  SELECT
    campaign_id,
    SUM(total_enrolled_member_count) AS matured_window_enr,
    SUM(\"30_day_dder_count\")         AS matured_window_dd_count
  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2
  WHERE platform = 'Google'
    AND campaign_id IN (SELECT campaign_id FROM campaign_ids)
    AND date BETWEEN (SELECT eff_start FROM eff) AND (SELECT dd_cutoff FROM eff)
  GROUP BY campaign_id
),
platform_matured AS (
  SELECT
    \"campaignId\"::text       AS campaign_id,
    SUM(\"costMicros\") / 1e6  AS matured_spend
  FROM google.reports_campaign_94
  WHERE customer_id = '7410524457'
    AND date >= (SELECT eff_start FROM eff)
    AND date <= (SELECT dd_cutoff FROM eff)
  GROUP BY \"campaignId\"
),
maturity AS (
  SELECT
    campaign_id,
    first_enroll_date,
    last_enroll_date,
    CASE
      WHEN last_enroll_date  + 30 <= (SELECT analysis_date FROM eff) THEN 'fully_mature'
      WHEN first_enroll_date + 30 <= (SELECT analysis_date FROM eff) THEN 'partially_mature'
      ELSE 'fully_immature'
    END AS maturity_stage
  FROM sot_current
),
hist_campaign AS (
  SELECT
    campaign_id,
    SUM(total_enrolled_member_count) AS matured_enr,
    SUM(\"30_day_dder_count\")         AS dd_count_mature
  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2
  WHERE platform = 'Google'
    AND campaign_id IN (SELECT campaign_id FROM campaign_ids)
    AND date <= (SELECT dd_cutoff FROM eff)
  GROUP BY campaign_id
),
campaign_types AS (
  SELECT
    ci.campaign_id,
    CASE
      WHEN LOWER(ci.campaign_name) LIKE '%uac%'
        OR LOWER(ci.campaign_name) LIKE '%admob%'    THEN 'UAC'
      WHEN LOWER(ci.campaign_name) LIKE '%discovery%'
        OR LOWER(ci.campaign_name) LIKE '%_dg_%'     THEN 'DemandGen'
      WHEN LOWER(ci.campaign_name) LIKE '%search%'   THEN 'Search'
      ELSE 'Other'
    END AS campaign_type
  FROM campaign_ids ci
),
hist_account AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(\"30_day_dder_count\")::float
      / NULLIF(SUM(total_enrolled_member_count), 0) AS rate
  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2
  WHERE platform = 'Google'
    AND campaign_id IN (SELECT campaign_id FROM campaign_ids)
    AND date <= (SELECT dd_cutoff FROM eff)
),
hist_same_type AS (
  SELECT
    ct.campaign_type,
    SUM(s.\"30_day_dder_count\")::float
      / NULLIF(SUM(s.total_enrolled_member_count), 0) AS rate
  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2 s

  WHERE s.platform = 'Google'
    AND s.campaign_id IN (SELECT campaign_id FROM campaign_ids)
    AND s.date <= (SELECT dd_cutoff FROM eff)
  GROUP BY ct.campaign_type

hist_rate AS (

    ci.campaign_id,

    COALESCE(hc.dd_count_mature, 0) AS dd_count_mature_hist,

        THEN hst.rate

  LEFT JOIN campaign_types ct     USING (campaign_id)
  LEFT JOIN hist_same_type hst    ON ct.campaign_type = hst.campaign_type
)

  ci.campaign_id,

  (SELECT eff_start    FROM eff)  AS eff_start,

  CASE
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'fully_mature'
      THEN ROUND((pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.dd_count_raw, 0))::numeric, 2)
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'partially_mature'
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_enr, 0) >= 500
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0) > 0
         AND pm.matured_spend IS NOT NULL
      THEN ROUND((pm.matured_spend / NULLIF(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0))::numeric, 2)
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                                    AS dd_cac,
  CASE
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'fully_mature'                              THEN 'full window'
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'partially_mature'
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_enr, 0) >= 500
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0) > 0                THEN 'matured slice'
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                                    AS dd_cac_source,
  ROUND((hr.hist_dd_rate * 100)::numeric, 2)                            AS hist_dd_rate_pct,
  hr.hist_rate_source,
  CASE
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'fully_mature'                              THEN NULL
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'partially_mature'
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_enr, 0) >= 500
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0) > 0                THEN NULL
    ELSE ROUND(((pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.enrollments, 0))
                / NULLIF(hr.hist_dd_rate, 0))::numeric, 2)
  END                                                                    AS expected_cac,
  mw.matured_window_enr,
  mw.matured_window_dd_count,
  ROUND(pm.matured_spend::numeric, 2)                                   AS matured_spend,
  (sc.campaign_id IS NOT NULL)                                           AS sot_matched,
  ROUND((pl.spend
    - (pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.enrollments, 0)) * sc.enrollments)::numeric, 2) AS cpe_sanity_diff,
  CASE WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'fully_mature'
    THEN ROUND((pl.spend
      - (pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.dd_count_raw, 0)) * sc.dd_count_raw)::numeric, 2)
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                                    AS ddcac_sanity_diff,
  CASE
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'partially_mature'
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_enr, 0) >= 500
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0) > 0
         AND pm.matured_spend IS NOT NULL
      THEN ROUND((pm.matured_spend
        - (pm.matured_spend / NULLIF(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0))
           * mw.matured_window_dd_count)::numeric, 4)
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                                    AS ddcac_matured_sanity_diff
FROM campaign_ids ci
JOIN platform    pl ON ci.campaign_id = pl.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN platform_matured pm ON ci.campaign_id = pm.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN sot_current      sc ON ci.campaign_id = sc.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN sot_matured_window mw ON ci.campaign_id = mw.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN maturity           m  ON ci.campaign_id = m.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN hist_rate          hr ON ci.campaign_id = hr.campaign_id
ORDER BY pl.spend DESC;
" --csv

## 1. Account Structure & Campaign Types

Google Structure & Campaign types:
- NB Search (Campaign name contains "nb_")
- Brand search (Campaign name contains "br_")
- Demand Gen Static (Campaign name contains "discovery", does NOT contain "video")
- YouTube (Campaign name contains "dg_video")
- UAC Android (Campaign name contains 'uac' or 'UAC', does NOT contain 'ios')
- UAC iOS (Campaign name contains 'IOS')
- Pmax (campaign name contains "performance max")

Offer vs BAU (breakout within campaign type):
- Intro Offer: Campaign name contains "offer" OR Labels value contains "offer"
- BAU: Everything else

Static vs Video (breakout within campaign type):
- Video: campaign name contains "video"
- Static: Everything else

Web Campaigns: Search Brand, Search Non-Brand, Demand Gen — all in ONE main Google Ads account.
App Campaigns: UAC (Universal App Campaigns) — split across MULTIPLE Google Ads accounts (iOS account, AdMob account, other properties). Same optimization strategy across all accounts, only targets differ.

## 2. Terminology Mapping

Equivalent Terms (Mean the Same Thing):
- Sign-ups = Enrollments = Enrolled Member Count
- CPE = Cost Per Enrollment = Cost per Sign-up
- In-app actions (AppsFlyer) = Enrollments = Participated in in-app actions
- DD = Direct Deposit
- DDCAC = DD CAC = Direct Deposit Customer Acquisition Cost
- DDR = DD Rate = Direct Deposit Rate

Non-Equivalent Terms (Different Things):
- Google's attributed enrollments ≠ Chime's attributed enrollments (different attribution methodology)
- Platform DD signal ≠ Backend DD data (platform DD has timestamp and match rate issues; backend DD is the source of truth)
- DSML predicted DD ≠ Actual 30-day DD (DSML is a Day-1 prediction; actual 30-day DD is observed outcome arriving 30 days later)

## 3. Primary Metrics by Campaign Type

Web Campaigns (Search + Demand Gen):
- Google Ads UI metric: "Sign-ups" column
- Cost metric: "Cost per Sign-ups"
- Sign-ups = Enrollments (same thing, different naming in platform)

App Campaigns (UAC):
- Google Ads UI metric: "Participated in in-app actions"
- Cost metric: "Cost per participated in in-app actions"
- Data source: AppsFlyer (piped into Google Ads)
- Equivalent to CPE

## 4. Campaign Structure Details

Ad Group Level: Mostly ONE ad group per campaign. Grouped by keyword themes. Optimization happens at CAMPAIGN level, not ad group level.

Keyword Themes/Categories: Checking, Bank, Competitor, Lower quality capture (fast cash, quick money).
Match Types Used: Exact match, Broad match.
Campaign Categories: Search Brand, Search Non-Brand, Demand Gen, UAC.
Offer Types (determined at ad level, not campaign level): Intro Offer, BAU (Business as Usual).

## 5. Attribution Methodology Differences

Offline Conversion Adjustment Pipeline:
- DSML predictive values are fed back into Google Ads via offline conversion adjustments
- This updates the "Sign Up" conversion action values retroactively
- Values are piped in next-day (not real-time)
- This is what allows non-brand search to use value-based bidding with predicted DD quality

Google Ads Platform Attribution:
- "Sign-ups" tracked via web pixel
- Google's own attribution model
- Metric name: "All Conversions Sign-ups"

Chime Internal Attribution (Looker/Backend):
- Metric name: "Total Enrolled Member Count"
- Last-click attribution, Chime's own methodology applied
- Other touchpoints can take credit over Google

Key point: Numbers between Google Ads and Looker will NOT match exactly. This is expected behavior, not an error.

## 6. Data Granularity & Limitations

Agent CAN analyze DD data at: Campaign level, Ad Group level, Keyword level (for added keywords only), Ad level.

Agent CANNOT analyze DD data at: Search query level (can only see keywords they match to, not the queries themselves), Placement level (UAC does not provide this data), Demographic level (UAC does not provide this data).

Keyword Data Limitation: Can only get reporting on ADDED keywords. Cannot get DD data on search queries directly. To track DD quality of a search term, must break it out as its own exact match keyword.

## 1. The DD Signal Problem (Critical Context)

Two DD data types exist in the ecosystem:

**Type 1: Actual 30-Day DD (Platform Signal)**
- Brand new, recently added to Google
- Issues: Timestamp problems, low match rate (click happened 30 days ago, matching back is unreliable)
- NOT currently used for optimization by the Chime team

**Type 2: DSML Predicted DD (Established Signal)**
- Established, been around for a while
- Day-1 prediction, values piped in next-day
- Used for non-brand ROAS bidding
- Signals: google_d0_binary_70e_9dd (binary) and value-based predictions

What channel managers actually use: Historical DD rates (from backend/Looker) + DSML predictions. NOT the actual 30-day DD counts in Google Ads platform.

**Critical rule**: The discrepancy between platform DD and backend DD is expected behavior. It is not a tracking issue. It is not a data quality problem. Do not flag it as an error or suggest MarTech investigation.

## 2. What Chime Wants

Primary goal: Reduction in DD CAC.

Secondary goals:
- Surface insights the team wasn't thinking of
- Identify new optimization strategies they haven't considered
- Identify opportunities to scale efficient campaigns
- Identify inefficient campaigns to cut
- Provide learnings beyond what the team is currently tracking

What they explicitly don't want:
- False alarms about data quality
- Confusion between platform metrics and backend metrics
- Recommendations requiring compliance review without acknowledging the blocker
- Panic about DD signal discrepancies

## 3. Decision Framework

### Step 0: Maturity Check (mandatory before any CAC calculation)

Before applying any CAC formula, determine whether the analysis period is mature or immature:

- **Mature period** (30-day DD window has closed; backend SOT DD count is stable and attributable):
  → Pull actual DD CAC = Spend ÷ DD Count directly from backend SOT
  → Use actual DD CAC for all scaling/cutting decisions below. **Skip Expected CAC entirely.**
  → Typical mature scenarios: completed calendar months, or any period where the full 30-day window has elapsed

- **Immature period** (30-day DD window has not yet closed; backend SOT DD counts are incomplete):
  → Proceed to Steps 1–4 below using Expected CAC
  → Typical immature scenarios: last 7 days, last 14 days, or any recent window where DD data has not matured

### Scaling Recommendations (immature periods — use Expected CAC):
1. Pull CPE for the campaign (from backend SOT enrollments + platform spend)
2. Pull the campaign's **historical DD rate** from backend SOT (the long-run established rate — NOT from the analysis window being studied)
3. Calculate Expected CAC = CPE / Historical DD Rate
4. Compare to monthly CAC goal
5. If Expected CAC < Goal → Recommend scaling

Action language: "Recommend reducing ROAS target by 5-10% to increase spend" / "This campaign has headroom to scale"

### Cutting Recommendations (immature periods — use Expected CAC):
1. Same Steps 1–3 as above
2. If Expected CAC > Goal → Recommend reducing spend

Action language: "Recommend raising ROAS target to reduce spend" / "Investigate DD quality drivers for this campaign"

### Scaling / Cutting Recommendations (mature periods — use actual DD CAC):
1. Pull actual DD CAC = Spend ÷ DD Count from backend SOT for the analysis period
2. Compare to monthly CAC goal
3. If actual DD CAC < Goal → Recommend scaling
4. If actual DD CAC > Goal → Recommend reducing spend

### Keyword Recommendations:
- Precondition: Keyword must have 60+ days of data (matured DD rate)
- Compare keyword DD rate to campaign average DD rate
- If significantly below average → Flag for pause or migration
- Do NOT recommend keyword pauses based on <60 days of data

## 4. Scope Boundaries

### In Scope:
- Campaign-level performance analysis
- CPE and Expected CAC calculations
- Scaling/cutting recommendations based on DD rate and CAC goal
- Keyword-level analysis (high-volume keywords, 60+ days data only)
- Flagging campaigns exceeding CAC goal or with headroom
- Surfacing insights across campaign types (Search Brand, Non-Brand, Demand Gen, UAC)
- Identifying DD rate trends per campaign

### Out of Scope (V1, may be added later):
- Search term level analysis (too granular, experience-dependent)
- Ad copy generation (compliance blocker exists)
- Extension optimization (not a priority)
- Placement-level insights for UAC (data does not exist)
- Demographic insights for UAC (data does not exist)

### Out of Scope (Permanently):
- Flagging DD signal discrepancies as errors
- Treating "Value" column as revenue (it's DSML predictions)
- Using platform DD signal as optimization input

## 5. Example Outputs

Good — Scaling:
"Campaign [Checking_NonBrand] has a CPE of $180 and historical DD rate of 28%. Expected CAC = $643, below the $800 monthly goal. This campaign has headroom. Recommend reducing ROAS target by 5-10% to increase spend."

Good — Quality Alert:
"Campaign [Competitor_Broad] DD rate has declined from 22% to 14% over the past 60 days while CPE remained flat at $175. Expected CAC has risen from $795 to $1,250. Recommend investigating keyword quality or reducing spend."

Bad — DD alarm (NEVER do this):
~~"There appears to be a data discrepancy between the DD signal in Google Ads and your backend data. This may indicate a tracking issue."~~
Why: The discrepancy is expected. This causes unnecessary escalations.

Bad — Treating Value as revenue (NEVER do this):
~~"Campaign [NonBrand_Checking] has generated $53,000 in revenue with $12,000 in spend, yielding a 4.4x ROAS."~~
Why: The $53,000 is DSML predicted DD value, not revenue.

## 6. Tone & Communication

- Be direct, not hedged. Say "Recommend reducing ROAS target" not "You might consider potentially looking at..."
- Be actionable. Every insight should have a clear next step.
- Be prioritized. Rank insights by impact on DD CAC. Lead with the biggest opportunity or problem.
- Do not create panic. Data discrepancies and signal differences are often expected behavior.
- Respect what the team already knows. Surface insights they may have missed, but don't explain basics.

cd /Users/mubi/htdocs/cursor-cli-agent/Pixis-Ai-Agent && bash ./tools/analyze-data.sh -c "
WITH
params AS (
  SELECT
    CURRENT_DATE                        AS analysis_date,
    CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days'   AS dd_cutoff,
    '2026-03-14'::date                  AS req_start,
    '2026-03-27'::date                  AS req_end
),
sot_range AS (
  SELECT MIN(date) AS sot_min, MAX(date) AS sot_max
  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2
  WHERE platform = 'Google'
),
eff AS (
  SELECT
    GREATEST(p.req_start, sr.sot_min) AS eff_start,
    LEAST(p.req_end,   sr.sot_max)    AS eff_end,
    p.dd_cutoff, p.analysis_date
  FROM params p, sot_range sr
),
campaign_ids AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT \"campaignId\" AS campaign_id, MAX(\"campaignName\") AS campaign_name
  FROM google.reports_campaign_94
  WHERE customer_id = '9494490746'
  GROUP BY \"campaignId\"
),
platform AS (
  SELECT
    \"campaignId\"::text       AS campaign_id,
    SUM(\"costMicros\") / 1e6  AS spend
  FROM google.reports_campaign_94
  WHERE customer_id = '9494490746'
    AND date >= (SELECT eff_start FROM eff)
    AND date <= (SELECT eff_end   FROM eff)
  GROUP BY \"campaignId\"
  HAVING SUM(\"costMicros\") > 0
),
sot_current AS (
  SELECT
    campaign_id,
    SUM(total_enrolled_member_count) AS enrollments,
    SUM(\"30_day_dder_count\")         AS dd_count_raw,
    MIN(date)                        AS first_enroll_date,
    MAX(date)                        AS last_enroll_date
  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2
  WHERE platform = 'Google'
    AND campaign_id IN (SELECT campaign_id FROM campaign_ids)
    AND date BETWEEN (SELECT eff_start FROM eff) AND (SELECT eff_end FROM eff)
  GROUP BY campaign_id
),
sot_matured_window AS (
  SELECT
    campaign_id,
    SUM(total_enrolled_member_count) AS matured_window_enr,
    SUM(\"30_day_dder_count\")         AS matured_window_dd_count
  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2
  WHERE platform = 'Google'
    AND campaign_id IN (SELECT campaign_id FROM campaign_ids)
    AND date BETWEEN (SELECT eff_start FROM eff) AND (SELECT dd_cutoff FROM eff)
  GROUP BY campaign_id
),
platform_matured AS (
  SELECT
    \"campaignId\"::text       AS campaign_id,
    SUM(\"costMicros\") / 1e6  AS matured_spend
  FROM google.reports_campaign_94
  WHERE customer_id = '9494490746'
    AND date >= (SELECT eff_start FROM eff)
    AND date <= (SELECT dd_cutoff FROM eff)
  GROUP BY \"campaignId\"
),
maturity AS (
  SELECT
    campaign_id,
    first_enroll_date,
    last_enroll_date,
    CASE
      WHEN last_enroll_date  + 30 <= (SELECT analysis_date FROM eff) THEN 'fully_mature'
      WHEN first_enroll_date + 30 <= (SELECT analysis_date FROM eff) THEN 'partially_mature'
      ELSE 'fully_immature'
    END AS maturity_stage
  FROM sot_current
),
hist_campaign AS (
  SELECT
    campaign_id,
    SUM(total_enrolled_member_count) AS matured_enr,
    SUM(\"30_day_dder_count\")         AS dd_count_mature
  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2
  WHERE platform = 'Google'
    AND campaign_id IN (SELECT campaign_id FROM campaign_ids)
    AND date <= (SELECT dd_cutoff FROM eff)
  GROUP BY campaign_id
),
campaign_types AS (
  SELECT
    ci.campaign_id,
    CASE
      WHEN LOWER(ci.campaign_name) LIKE '%uac%'
        OR LOWER(ci.campaign_name) LIKE '%admob%'    THEN 'UAC'
      WHEN LOWER(ci.campaign_name) LIKE '%discovery%'
        OR LOWER(ci.campaign_name) LIKE '%_dg_%'     THEN 'DemandGen'
      WHEN LOWER(ci.campaign_name) LIKE '%search%'   THEN 'Search'
      ELSE 'Other'
    END AS campaign_type
  FROM campaign_ids ci
),
hist_account AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(\"30_day_dder_count\")::float
      / NULLIF(SUM(total_enrolled_member_count), 0) AS rate
  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2
  WHERE platform = 'Google'
    AND campaign_id IN (SELECT campaign_id FROM campaign_ids)
    AND date <= (SELECT dd_cutoff FROM eff)
),
hist_same_type AS (
  SELECT
    ct.campaign_type,
    SUM(s.\"30_day_dder_count\")::float
      / NULLIF(SUM(s.total_enrolled_member_count), 0) AS rate
  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2 s
  JOIN campaign_types ct USING (campaign_id)
  WHERE s.platform = 'Google'
    AND s.campaign_id IN (SELECT campaign_id FROM campaign_ids)
    AND s.date <= (SELECT dd_cutoff FROM eff)
  GROUP BY ct.campaign_type
),
hist_rate AS (
  SELECT
    ci.campaign_id,
    COALESCE(hc.matured_enr, 0) AS matured_enr,
    COALESCE(hc.dd_count_mature, 0) AS dd_count_mature_hist,
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(hc.matured_enr, 0) >= 500
        THEN hc.dd_count_mature::float / NULLIF(hc.matured_enr, 0)
      WHEN COALESCE(hc.matured_enr, 0) >= 100
        THEN hst.rate
      ELSE
        (SELECT rate FROM hist_account)
    END AS hist_dd_rate,
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(hc.matured_enr, 0) >= 500 THEN '(a) campaign own'
      WHEN COALESCE(hc.matured_enr, 0) >= 100 THEN '(b) same-type'
      ELSE                                          '(c) account-wide'
    END AS hist_rate_source
  FROM campaign_ids ci
  LEFT JOIN hist_campaign hc      USING (campaign_id)
  LEFT JOIN campaign_types ct     USING (campaign_id)
  LEFT JOIN hist_same_type hst    ON ct.campaign_type = hst.campaign_type
)
SELECT
  ci.campaign_id,
  ci.campaign_name,
  (SELECT eff_start    FROM eff)  AS eff_start,
  (SELECT eff_end      FROM eff)  AS eff_end,
  (SELECT dd_cutoff    FROM eff)  AS dd_cutoff,
  (SELECT analysis_date FROM eff) AS analysis_date,
  ROUND(pl.spend::numeric, 2)     AS spend,
  sc.enrollments,
  sc.dd_count_raw,
  m.maturity_stage,
  m.first_enroll_date,
  m.last_enroll_date,
  hr.matured_enr,
  hr.dd_count_mature_hist,
  ROUND((pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.enrollments, 0))::numeric, 2)             AS cpe,
  CASE
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'fully_mature'
      THEN ROUND((pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.dd_count_raw, 0))::numeric, 2)
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'partially_mature'
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_enr, 0) >= 500
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0) > 0
         AND pm.matured_spend IS NOT NULL
      THEN ROUND((pm.matured_spend / NULLIF(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0))::numeric, 2)
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                                    AS dd_cac,
  CASE
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'fully_mature'                              THEN 'full window'
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'partially_mature'
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_enr, 0) >= 500
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0) > 0                THEN 'matured slice'
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                                    AS dd_cac_source,
  ROUND((hr.hist_dd_rate * 100)::numeric, 2)                            AS hist_dd_rate_pct,
  hr.hist_rate_source,
  CASE
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'fully_mature'                              THEN NULL
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'partially_mature'
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_enr, 0) >= 500
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0) > 0                THEN NULL
    ELSE ROUND(((pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.enrollments, 0))
                / NULLIF(hr.hist_dd_rate, 0))::numeric, 2)
  END                                                                    AS expected_cac,
  mw.matured_window_enr,
  mw.matured_window_dd_count,
  ROUND(pm.matured_spend::numeric, 2)                                   AS matured_spend,
  (sc.campaign_id IS NOT NULL)                                           AS sot_matched,
  ROUND((pl.spend
    - (pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.enrollments, 0)) * sc.enrollments)::numeric, 2) AS cpe_sanity_diff,
  CASE WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'fully_mature'
    THEN ROUND((pl.spend
      - (pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.dd_count_raw, 0)) * sc.dd_count_raw)::numeric, 2)
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                                    AS ddcac_sanity_diff,
  CASE
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'partially_mature'
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_enr, 0) >= 500
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0) > 0
         AND pm.matured_spend IS NOT NULL
      THEN ROUND((pm.matured_spend
        - (pm.matured_spend / NULLIF(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0))
           * mw.matured_window_dd_count)::numeric, 4)
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                                    AS ddcac_matured_sanity_diff
FROM campaign_ids ci
JOIN platform    pl ON ci.campaign_id = pl.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN platform_matured pm ON ci.campaign_id = pm.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN sot_current      sc ON ci.campaign_id = sc.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN sot_matured_window mw ON ci.campaign_id = mw.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN maturity           m  ON ci.campaign_id = m.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN hist_rate          hr ON ci.campaign_id = hr.campaign_id
ORDER BY pl.spend DESC;
" --csv 2>/dev/null

  SELECT
    campaign_id,

  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2

         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_enr, 0) >= 500

         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_enr, 0) >= 500

  ROUND((pl.spend
    - (pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.enrollments, 0)) * sc.enrollments)::numeric, 2) AS cpe_sanity_diff,
  CASE WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'fully_mature'
    THEN ROUND((pl.spend
      - (pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.dd_count_raw, 0)) * sc.dd_count_raw)::numeric, 2)
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                                    AS ddcac_sanity_diff,
  CASE
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'partially_mature'
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_enr, 0) >= 500
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0) > 0
         AND pm.matured_spend IS NOT NULL
      THEN ROUND((pm.matured_spend
        - (pm.matured_spend / NULLIF(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0))

  END                                                                    AS ddcac_matured_sanity_diff

JOIN platform    pl ON ci.campaign_id = pl.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN platform_matured pm ON ci.campaign_id = pm.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN sot_current      sc ON ci.campaign_id = sc.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN sot_matured_window mw ON ci.campaign_id = mw.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN maturity           m  ON ci.campaign_id = m.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN hist_rate          hr ON ci.campaign_id = hr.campaign_id
ORDER BY pl.spend DESC;
"

  SELECT MIN(date) AS sot_min, MAX(date) AS sot_max
  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2
  WHERE platform = 'Google'
),
eff AS (
  SELECT
    GREATEST(p.req_start, sr.sot_min) AS eff_start,
    LEAST(p.req_end,   sr.sot_max)    AS eff_end,
    p.dd_cutoff, p.analysis_date
  FROM params p, sot_range sr
),
campaign_ids AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT \"campaignId\" AS campaign_id, MAX(\"campaignName\") AS campaign_name
  FROM google.reports_campaign_94
  WHERE customer_id = '9494490746'
  GROUP BY \"campaignId\"
),
platform AS (
  SELECT
    \"campaignId\"::text       AS campaign_id,
    SUM(\"costMicros\") / 1e6  AS spend
  FROM google.reports_campaign_94
  WHERE customer_id = '9494490746'
    AND date >= (SELECT eff_start FROM eff)
    AND date <= (SELECT eff_end   FROM eff)
  GROUP BY \"campaignId\"
  HAVING SUM(\"costMicros\") > 0
),
sot_current AS (
  SELECT
    campaign_id,
    SUM(total_enrolled_member_count) AS enrollments,
    SUM(\"30_day_dder_count\")         AS dd_count_raw,
    MIN(date)                        AS first_enroll_date,
    MAX(date)                        AS last_enroll_date
  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2
  WHERE platform = 'Google'
    AND campaign_id IN (SELECT campaign_id FROM campaign_ids)
    AND date BETWEEN (SELECT eff_start FROM eff) AND (SELECT eff_end FROM eff)
  GROUP BY campaign_id
),
sot_matured_window AS (
  SELECT
    campaign_id,
    SUM(total_enrolled_member_count) AS matured_window_enr,
    SUM(\"30_day_dder_count\")         AS matured_window_dd_count
  FROM google_sheets.google_sheet_dump_94_2
  WHERE platform = 'Google'
    AND campaign_id IN (SELECT campaign_id FROM campaign_ids)
    AND date BETWEEN (SELECT eff_start FROM eff) AND (SELECT dd_cutoff FROM eff)
  GROUP BY campaign_id
),
platform_matured AS (
  SELECT
    \"campaignId\"::text       AS campaign_id,
    SUM(\"costMicros\") / 1e6  AS matured_spend
  FROM google.reports_campaign_94
  WHERE customer_id = '9494490746'
    AND date >= (SELECT eff_start FROM eff)
    AND date <= (SELECT dd_cutoff FROM eff)
  GROUP BY \"campaignId\"
),
maturity AS (
  SELECT
    campaign_id,

    last_enroll_date,
    CASE
      WHEN last_enroll_date  + 30 <= (SELECT analysis_date FROM eff) THEN 'fully_mature'

      ELSE 'fully_immature'
    END AS maturity_stage

),
hist_campaign AS (

    campaign_id,

),

        THEN hst.rate

    END AS hist_dd_rate,

      WHEN COALESCE(hc.matured_enr, 0) >= 500 THEN '(a) campaign own'

SELECT
  ci.campaign_id,
  ci.campaign_name,
  (SELECT eff_start    FROM eff)  AS eff_start,
  (SELECT eff_end      FROM eff)  AS eff_end,
  (SELECT dd_cutoff    FROM eff)  AS dd_cutoff,

  m.maturity_stage,
  m.first_enroll_date,
  m.last_enroll_date,
  hr.matured_enr,
  hr.dd_count_mature_hist,
  ROUND((pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.enrollments, 0))::numeric, 2)             AS cpe,
  CASE
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'fully_mature'
      THEN ROUND((pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.dd_count_raw, 0))::numeric, 2)
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'partially_mature'
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_enr, 0) >= 500
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0) > 0
         AND pm.matured_spend IS NOT NULL
      THEN ROUND((pm.matured_spend / NULLIF(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0))::numeric, 2)
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                                    AS dd_cac,
  CASE
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'fully_mature'                              THEN 'full window'
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'partially_mature'
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_enr, 0) >= 500
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0) > 0                THEN 'matured slice'
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                                    AS dd_cac_source,
  ROUND((hr.hist_dd_rate * 100)::numeric, 2)                            AS hist_dd_rate_pct,
  hr.hist_rate_source,
  CASE
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'fully_mature'                              THEN NULL
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'partially_mature'
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_enr, 0) >= 500
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0) > 0                THEN NULL
    ELSE ROUND(((pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.enrollments, 0))
                / NULLIF(hr.hist_dd_rate, 0))::numeric, 2)
  END                                                                    AS expected_cac,
  mw.matured_window_enr,
  mw.matured_window_dd_count,
  ROUND(pm.matured_spend::numeric, 2)                                   AS matured_spend,
  (sc.campaign_id IS NOT NULL)                                           AS sot_matched,
  ROUND((pl.spend
    - (pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.enrollments, 0)) * sc.enrollments)::numeric, 2) AS cpe_sanity_diff,
  CASE WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'fully_mature'
    THEN ROUND((pl.spend
      - (pl.spend / NULLIF(sc.dd_count_raw, 0)) * sc.dd_count_raw)::numeric, 2)
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                                    AS ddcac_sanity_diff,
  CASE
    WHEN m.maturity_stage = 'partially_mature'
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_enr, 0) >= 500
         AND COALESCE(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0) > 0
         AND pm.matured_spend IS NOT NULL
      THEN ROUND((pm.matured_spend
        - (pm.matured_spend / NULLIF(mw.matured_window_dd_count, 0))
           * mw.matured_window_dd_count)::numeric, 4)
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                                    AS ddcac_matured_sanity_diff
FROM campaign_ids ci
JOIN platform    pl ON ci.campaign_id = pl.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN platform_matured pm ON ci.campaign_id = pm.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN sot_current      sc ON ci.campaign_id = sc.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN sot_matured_window mw ON ci.campaign_id = mw.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN maturity           m  ON ci.campaign_id = m.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN hist_rate          hr ON ci.campaign_id = hr.campaign_id
ORDER BY pl.spend DESC;
" --csv
